Monitoring Documentation

How user behavior tracking works, what's protected, and how to diagnose issues

Monitoring Documentation

How user behavior tracking works, what's protected, and how to diagnose issues

System Overview

Two complementary tools for complete visibility

PostHog

Product analytics, session replay, heatmaps, and funnel analysis

  • Session recordings
  • Funnel conversion tracking
  • Event analytics

Error Tracker

Custom error tracking stored in Supabase (view at /admin/error-logs)

  • JavaScript error capture
  • Error fingerprinting and deduplication
  • Session linking with PostHog

Privacy & Compliance

Data protection measures in place

Always Masked (Never Captured)

  • • All form input values
  • • Passwords and authentication tokens
  • • Email addresses in forms
  • • Phone numbers
  • • Physical addresses
  • • Payment/credit card details
  • • SSN or government IDs

What IS Tracked

  • • Page URLs and navigation paths
  • • Button clicks and element interactions
  • • Scroll depth and time on page
  • • Device type, browser, OS
  • • Form field names (not values)
  • • Error messages (sanitized)
  • • API response times

Cookie Consent

Users see a consent banner on first visit. They can choose "Accept All" for full analytics, "Essential Only" for basic functionality, or decline entirely. We respect Do Not Track headers.

Events Tracked

Standard event schema for analytics

Event Properties Trigger
page_viewurl, referrer, utm_*Route change
form_startform_name, pageFirst field focus
form_submit_attemptform_nameSubmit click
form_submit_successform_name, response_time_msSuccessful submission
form_submit_failureform_name, error_categoryFailed submission
quote_step_viewedstep_name, step_indexQuote step navigation
exit_intenttime_on_page, scroll_depth, had_errorMouse leaves viewport / tab switch
rage_clickelement_selector, click_count3+ rapid clicks on same element
web_vitalslcp_ms, inp_ms, clsAfter page load

Debugging Drop-offs

How to diagnose why users exit or forms fail

1. Check Funnels in PostHog

Go to PostHog → Funnels. Look at the Quote and Contact form funnels to see which step has the highest drop-off rate. Segment by device/browser to find patterns.

2. Watch Session Replays

Filter sessions by users who had form_submit_failure events. Watch what they did before the error. Look for rage clicks or confusion.

3. Check Error Logs

If a user encountered an error, their PostHog session ID is stored with the error log. Visit /admin/error-logs and search by session ID to find the exact error.

4. Check Exit Intent Data

The exit_intent event captures whether an error occurred in the last 60 seconds before exit. Filter for had_error_recently = true.

This is an orientation map, not a build spec. Live nodes open the real admin page. Documented nodes cite the actual mechanism with no dedicated screen. Planned nodes (dashed) describe a step that does not exist yet — click any node for detail.

Constraint — business rule: first-submit intake stays minimal (name, email/phone, one or two qualifiers) to protect ad conversion. Anything beyond that moves to the BQA step below, not the initial form.
Constraint — documented: every submit is deduped via submission_fingerprint (md5 of email + format + quantity + message + service_type), minute-bucketed as a unique index. A collision returns the existing lead instead of erroring — a double-submit reads as "success, once," not a new record.
